claims.claim: Argentina's National Institute of Statistics and Census reported that poverty reached 32.3 percent of people in the first half of 2026, up 4.1 percentage points from the second half of 2025.
claims.episode_span: poverty reached 32.3 percent of people in the first half of 2026, 4.1 points above the second half of 2025
claims.source_title: Poverty in Argentina rises to 32.3%, ending two years of decline
claims.supporting_quote: Poverty in Argentina reached 32.3% of people in the first half of 2026, an increase of 4.1 percentage points on the second half of 2025, the National Institute of Statistics and Census reported on Thursday.

claims.claim: Extreme poverty in Argentina rose from 6.3 percent to 7.5 percent.
claims.episode_span: Extreme poverty rose 1.2 points, from 6.3 percent to 7.5 percent.
claims.source_title: Poverty in Argentina rises to 32.3%, ending two years of decline
claims.supporting_quote: Extreme poverty rose 1.2 points, from 6.3% to 7.5%.

claims.claim: In 31 urban agglomerations, 9,729,000 people were below the poverty line and 2,249,000 below the extreme poverty line.
claims.episode_span: 9,729,000 people were below the poverty line and 2,249,000 below the extreme poverty line
claims.source_title: Poverty in Argentina rises to 32.3%, ending two years of decline
claims.supporting_quote: The measurement covers the 31 urban agglomerations surveyed by the Permanent Household Survey, where 9,729,000 people fell below the poverty line and 2,249,000 below the extreme poverty line.

claims.claim: Argentine media estimates put national poverty at 15.4 to 15.5 million people and extreme poverty at about 3.6 million.
claims.episode_span: national figures at 15.4 to 15.5 million people in poverty and about 3.6 million in extreme poverty
claims.source_title: Poverty in Argentina rises to 32.3%, ending two years of decline
claims.supporting_quote: Projected to the country as a whole, estimates published by Argentine media place the figure at between 15.4 and 15.5 million people in poverty and around 3.6 million in extreme poverty.

claims.claim: In June a family of four in Argentina needed 1,531,473 pesos to stay above the poverty line and 689,853 pesos to avoid extreme poverty.
claims.episode_span: a family of four needed 1,531,473 pesos to stay above the poverty line and 689,853 pesos to avoid extreme poverty
claims.source_title: Poverty in Argentina rises to 32.3%, ending two years of decline
claims.supporting_quote: In June, a family of four needed 1,531,473 pesos to stay above the poverty line and 689,853 to avoid extreme poverty.

claims.claim: Hurricane Polo had maximum sustained winds of around 150 mph, and a reading of 892 millibars on 22 September made it the second-most intense hurricane on record in the east Pacific.
claims.episode_span: maximum sustained winds of around 150 miles per hour
claims.source_title: Hurricane Polo barrels towards Baja California region of Mexico
claims.supporting_quote: On 22 September, a measurement of 892 millibars was registered for Hurricane Polo, making it the second-most intense hurricane on record in the east Pacific.

claims.claim: The UN Group of Human Rights Experts on Nicaragua detailed 161 enforced disappearances since April 2018 in a report published on 21 September.
claims.episode_span: details 161 cases of enforced disappearance since April 2018
claims.source_title: ‘Anatomy of State Cruelty’: UN report alleges deliberate and escalating rights abuses in Nicaragua
claims.supporting_quote: The 47-page dossier published on September 21 detailed 161 cases of enforced disappearance in the country since April 2018, when protests over social security reforms widened into a national challenge to Daniel Ortega’s government and were met with a violent crackdown that left more than 300 people dead.

claims.claim: Authorities announced the death of Miskito leader Brooklyn Rivera Bryan on 31 May.
claims.episode_span: Brooklyn Rivera Bryan, 73, whose death authorities announced on 31 May
claims.source_title: ‘Anatomy of State Cruelty’: UN report alleges deliberate and escalating rights abuses in Nicaragua
claims.supporting_quote: The dossier profiles eight individuals who were detained on political grounds and died “preventable deaths” in state custody as a result of inhumane treatment, paying particular attention to the case of 73-year-old Miskito Indigenous leader Brooklyn Rivera Bryan, whose death was announced by authorities on May 31 of this year.
